questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the destination was different to my everyday life back in copenhagen. I wanted a destination where I had the opportunity of exploring a lot of the country, and it had to be warm.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to some extend, the university had a great website, and they send a lot of information to internation/exchange students before arrival with tips on how to find accommodation and how to apply for visa, and other necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation week which was very helpful, as it gave important information if there was any doubt about anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just googled student accommodation in brisbane and found a lot. Later the university provided a list. I would recommend finding a private flat to live in, if you are willing to wait until arrival to find one. Otherwise there is a lot of great student accommodations in Brisbane, which I enjoyed staying at like Westella, StudenOne and Igloo.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Publuc transportation in brisbane is only 2kr per trip, and it is very easy to get to campus from cbd. It is nice to stay in cbd or nearby as this is close to the beach.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They send you an email with steps you have to follow. You have to be careful, if you want to take courses on another faculty, then the university has to accept you before you are able to enrol in those. I would recommend talking to the university before registrating, as it becomes less stressful, but it worked out very easily for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a contact person, who was very helpful in answering questions and assisting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Flow the instructions provided. If you need an english test, do it in advance as it will make the registration process smoother.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to Denmark, but less theoretical. There was a lot of assignments during the semester, but that made the exam period a bit easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All of the lectures are uploaded online, which is nice, because you don't have to worry about lectures being held at the same time. You can choose a lot of different time slots for the tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Economics of Climate Change
Big Data And Machine Learning for Economics and Finance
Further Topics in Operations Research
Economics of Financial Markets

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Big Data And Machine Learning for Economics and Finance - Less theoretical coding course, which was nice to see. 
Further Topics in Operations Research - Small course and fun topics. Learned a lot of python from this course. 
Economics of Financial Markets - A mix between macroeconomics and finance.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, but public transportation is so cheap in Brisbane, that it wasn't a cost. Food prices are similar to Denmark. In a lot of student accommodations you need to buy some kitchen utensils.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportion to campus. 

I uses a lot of money each month on going on weekend trips all around australia.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Join the mountain-climbing club!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but they provide information on everything in the market day in the orientation week, or on their instagram.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the mountain-climbing club. They organise hikes, and climbing trips. I had never been rock-climbing before, but every Tuesday and thursday you can try rock-climbing in brisbane for free if you are a member.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whitsundays, Cairns (great barrier reef), Vanuatu, Gold Coast, Byron Bay!, Noosa (2 kr public transportation to this place). New Zealand for the mid-sem break, uluru.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are very nice in Australia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some of the clubs, and participate in the orientation week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How kind people are. It is a very laid back culture, and very active.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go on a lot of trips. Plan your schedule so that you have consecutive days off, or in connection with the weekend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Brisbane has nice weather all year, while some other australian destinations may be a bit colder.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the memories and friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: FInding enough time for all the fun trips.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
